# Observations Log

## 2026-08-01 — Public certificate page displays WRONG certificate numbers (client-side last-4-digit truncation) — 18 of 67 public certs affected; strongest candidate for the client's "can't find it when I search" complaint

**Context:** Shawn could not reproduce the client's reported filtering issue with the `main.js` redirect defect (logged 2026-07-31, fixed). Ran a broader sweep of the public tile page in test. **The filter/query layer passed every test** (see "sweep results" below) — but the sweep surfaced a different, more likely culprit.

### The defect

**`wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view.js:1247-1250` — `formatCertificateNumber()` falls through to a last-4-digits truncation:**
```js
const numbers = certificateNumber.replace(/\D/g, '');
if (numbers) {
    const paddedNumber = numbers.slice(-4).padStart(4, '0');   // <-- silently drops digits
    return `${year}-${paddedNumber}`;
}
```
A certificate number with a **5-digit suffix** (e.g. `26-10136`) matches neither `^\d{2}-\d{4}$` (line 1222) nor `^\d+$` (line 1241), so it reaches line 1247: digits become `2610136`, `.slice(-4)` → `0136`, and the card **displays `26-0136`** — a number that does not exist.

**The API is correct.** `/api/certificate-tiles` returns `certificateNumber: "26-10136"`; the server's own `FormatCertificateNumber` (`CertificateTilesApiController.cs:42-62`) has **no** last-4 branch and correctly returns the value as-is. The corruption is introduced purely by the redundant **client-side re-format** at `createCertificateCard()` line 467.

**Scope — 18 of 67 public certificates (27%) display a wrong number:** `26-10136, 10135, 10128, 10127, 10125, 10118, 10115, 10109, 10106, 10100, 10091, 10088, 10082, 10079, 10064, 10061, 10055, 10052` → all shown with the `1` dropped (`26-0136`, `26-0135`, …).

### Why this produces a "filtering/search is broken" report

The card's **click handler passes the real number** (`onclick="viewCertificateDetails('26-10136')"`, line 478) while the card **body displays the truncated one** (line 478 text node). So clicking works fine and opens the right certificate — but the number the user can *read* is wrong. Verified live:

| User action | Result |
|---|---|
| `search=26-0136` (the number printed on the card) | **0 results** |
| `search=26-10136` (the real number) | 1 result |
| `search=0136` (partial) | 1 result |

So the client sees a certificate on screen, types the number shown on it, and gets **"No certificates found."** That is a search/filter complaint whose root cause is a *display* bug — which is exactly why it can't be reproduced by driving the filter controls. DOM scan confirmed 18/50 tiles on page 1 have `displayed !== onclick value`.

**Open question for the client/requirements:** whether `26-10136` is itself valid. The documented format is **YY-NNNN** (4 digits); these test records carry 5-digit suffixes (10052–10136), which the format cannot represent. Two readings: (a) the JS must stop truncating and display the true stored value, or (b) the underlying numbers are out-of-range test data. **Recommended fix regardless: delete the client-side re-format and render `cert.certificateNumber` straight from the API** — the server already formatted it, and the table-row renderer at js:1474 already does exactly this (`escapeHtml(cert.certificateNumber || '')`). That removes the server/client disagreement rather than duplicating format logic in two places. Related to Shawn's standing question about certs pages showing ID vs certificate number. **NOT yet fixed — awaiting Shawn's call.**

### Sweep results — filtering itself is CLEAN (UI totals verified against direct API calls, live)

Every case below matched exactly (UI `Showing N of N` vs `totalCount` for the equivalent API query): no filters (68); country US (34); country US+Canada (35); certType Recycled Content (8); two cert types (11); company 3M (2); **company containing a comma** — General Mills, Inc. (2); **company containing comma + ampersand** — ASSA ABLOY … Corbin Russwin Division (1); category L1 Chemicals (60); L2 Plastics (3); **L3 HDPE (2)**; L1 containing a comma — Electronics, Computers, and Accessories (2); tag APR (3); certType + country cross-facet (5); and a legitimately-empty combination (certType Recycled + country Germany → 0, correct "No certificates found" empty state).

Also verified clean:
- **Delimiter safety** — audited all 90 filter option values: **zero contain `|`**; 6 contain commas, none on the comma-split (tags) path. The `|` join is not colliding with real data today.
- **Deep-link / refresh restore** — `/?category=Plastics&country=United+States&sort=company-az` restored both checkboxes, both chips, the "Company A-Z" sort label, and the correct 2 results.

### Noted, not fixed — filters create no browser history

Applying three filters produced **0 new history entries** (`history.length` 12 → 12) because `updateUrl()` uses `history.replaceState` (js:936). Back therefore does not undo a filter — it leaves the page entirely. Deep links and refresh work correctly (above), so this is a UX judgment call, not a data bug. Flagging in case the client's "it resets" wording is actually about the Back button.

## 2026-07-31 — Public certificate page "filtering issues" — ROOT CAUSE = `main.js` global search handler hard-navigates and wipes every active filter (diagnosis only, no code changed)

**Report (Shawn):** filtering issues on gccwebapp.com, public certificate tile page; symptom described as "filter resets or errors."

### ROOT CAUSE (reproduced live, confirmed by controlled A/B on the deployed site)

**`wwwroot/js/main.js:310-344` — `initializeSearchFunctionality()` binds a global Enter handler to `.search-bar input`, which IS the public page's own search box. On Enter it calls `performSearch()` → `window.location.href = '/Certificate/CertificateTileView?search=' + query` (line 342) — a FULL PAGE NAVIGATION carrying ONLY the search term. Every active filter (cert type, product category, company, country, tags) and the sort are silently discarded.**

`main.js:313-317` has a guard that is supposed to prevent exactly this:
```js
const isTileViewPage = window.location.pathname.toLowerCase().includes('/certificate/certificatetileview');
if (isTileViewPage) return;   // "Skip on Certificate tile view pages - they have their own search handling"
```
**The guard tests `pathname`, but the public tile view is served at the site ROOT `/`** (default route, `Program.cs:857` — `{controller=Certificate}/{action=CertificateTileView}/{id?}`). A visitor on `https://gccwebapp.com/` has `pathname === '/'`, which does **not** contain `/certificate/certificatetileview`, so the guard misses, `main.js` binds its handler alongside the page's own Enter handler in `certificate-tile-view.js:781-796`, and the hard redirect wins.

**Why it looks intermittent/maddening:** after that redirect the URL *is* `/Certificate/CertificateTileView`, so the guard now matches and Enter behaves correctly from then on. **The bug only fires on the first search of a session from the homepage — which is how every public visitor arrives.**

**Controlled proof on the deployed site (same tab, same build):**
| Page | Guard matches? | Set country=United States, then Enter "3M" | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` (root) | **no** | page marker WIPED, `navType: "navigate"` | filters gone — checkboxes `[]`, chips `["3M"]`, URL `?search=3M` only |
| `/Certificate/CertificateTileView` | yes | page marker `ALIVE` (no navigation) | correct — checkboxes `["United States"]`, chips `["3M","United States"]`, URL keeps both |

Also confirmed `document.querySelector('.search-bar input') === document.querySelector('.search-input')` → **true**, i.e. `main.js` is binding to the page's own search box. Deployed `certificate-tile-view.js` verified byte-consistent with the working tree (63,572 bytes / 1,529 lines).

**FIX APPLIED (Shawn approved option A, 2026-07-31) — `wwwroot/js/main.js:313-325`.** The guard now detects the PAGE, not the URL:
```js
const isTileViewPage = window.location.pathname.toLowerCase().includes('/certificate/certificatetileview')
    || document.getElementById('certificatesGrid') !== null;
```
`#certificatesGrid` is present on all three tile views (`CertificateTileView.cshtml:192`, `...External.cshtml:206`, `...Internal.cshtml:274`) **and nowhere else** — and `.search-bar` likewise exists only in those same three views, so `initializeSearchFunctionality()`/`performSearch()` were already effectively dead code on every other page. `initializeSearchFunctionality()` runs on `DOMContentLoaded` (`main.js:20`), so the grid element is parsed and present when the guard evaluates. JS-only, one-line logic change, no markup or server change, pending next deploy bundle.

**Verified on the deployed site (live, root `/`):** old guard → `false` (the bug); new guard → `true` (skips). Then simulated the fixed state by neutralizing `performSearch` and replaying the failing scenario from `/`: tick **United States** (34 results) → type `3M` → Enter → **page survived, no navigation**, results correctly narrowed to **2**, checkbox `["United States"]` retained, chips `["3M","United States"]`, URL kept both params. Same scenario pre-fix wiped the checkbox and dropped `country` from the URL.

**Per Shawn: no search bar/button is being added (design decision).** The secondary defect below therefore stands as accepted behavior for now — a typed term is still discarded unless Enter is pressed. If it is revisited later, the fix that respects the no-button constraint is committing the search on **blur** (and/or debounced input), not adding a control.

### Secondary defect (same page, independent of the above)

**A typed search is silently discarded unless Enter is pressed.** There is no search button; `certificate-tile-view.js:749-751` deliberately commits only on Enter or suggestion-click. Reproduced: type `3M` (no Enter) → grid still shows all 68; then tick **United States** → grid shows **34** (all US certs, un-searched) **while the box still visibly reads "3M"** and no chip is drawn. The user sees a search term sitting in the box and results that plainly ignore it — reads as "the filter reset." Recommend committing on blur/debounced input, or adding a visible search button.

### CORRECTION — rate limiting is NOT the cause (earlier hypothesis, retracted)

An initial pass attributed this to `IpRateLimiting` (`*/api/*`, 100/min, `Program.cs:646-649`). **That attribution was wrong and is retracted.** `appsettings.json` sets **`EnableEndpointRateLimiting: true`**, which gives **each endpoint its own counter** — saturating `/api/certificate-tiles/autocomplete` does **not** throttle `/api/certificate-tiles`. Verified live: a 120-request parallel burst returned 60×200 / 60×429 on autocomplete, and the very next checkbox filter still loaded correctly (5→8 certs, right numbers). Rate limiting is real but only degrades the **autocomplete dropdown**, not the grid filtering.

### Still worth fixing (verified, lower priority)

- **Autocomplete debounce is dead code.** `state.debounceTimer` is declared (js:24) and `clearTimeout`'d (js:731) but **never assigned a `setTimeout`** — confirmed in the deployed bundle. Live measurement: typing a 16-character search fired **15** `/autocomplete` calls. That is what makes the 100/min autocomplete bucket reachable at all; a ~300ms debounce removes the problem.
- **No 429 handling.** `loadCertificates` retries only on 5xx (js:294-300); a 429 is terminal — grid keeps stale tiles, `#resultsCount` stays pinned at `"Loading…"`. Deployed bundle contains no reference to `429` or `Retry-After`.
- **Tag separator mismatch (latent).** `buildApiParams()` joins tags with `'|'` (js:362-367); `CertificateTilesApiController.cs:162` splits on `','`. Selecting **2+ external tags** yields a bogus tag name → `__INVALID_TAG_FILTER__` sentinel (lines 170-173) → **guaranteed 0 results**. Masked today only because the DB has exactly one external tag (`APR`).
- **Offset/limit truncation (latent).** `Page = (actualOffset / actualLimit) + 1` integer division (controller:115) vs. client advancing `loadedCount` by **de-duplicated** count (js:270-279) — once `loadedCount` stops being a multiple of the 50-item batch, infinite scroll stalls with `hasMore` stuck true. Not reachable at 68 records.
- **All controller failures return 400, not 500** (lines 220-243, 414-418, 509-524), routing genuine server errors into the same no-retry branch as a 429.

### What was ruled OUT

The filter/query layer is correct — verified live against `/api/certificate-tiles` (the test gate exempts `/api`). Baseline 68 public certs; `country=United States` → 34, `+Canada` → 35, `certType=Recycled Content` → 8, two cert types → 11, `company=3M|Acme Corporation` → 4, `search=Best` → 4, `tags=APR` → 3, `certType + country` → 5. Hierarchical categories resolve at all three levels (L1 Chemicals 60, L2 Metal Alloys 3, L2 Plastics 3, L3 HDPE 2, L3 PET 1). Paging returns 68 unique IDs across offset 0/50 with no duplicates and `hasMore` flipping false correctly. The repository predicate, alias coalescing, and public status/expiry pinning all behave.

**What was ruled OUT (verified live against `/api/certificate-tiles`, which the test gate exempts):** the filter/query layer is correct. Baseline 68 public certs; `country=United States` → 34, `country=United States|Canada` → 35, `certType=Recycled Content` → 8, two cert types → 11, `company=3M|Acme Corporation` → 4, `search=Best` → 4, `tags=APR` → 3, cross-facet `certType + country` → 5. Hierarchical product categories resolve at all three levels (L1 Chemicals 60, L2 Metal Alloys 3, L2 Plastics 3, L3 HDPE 2, L3 PET 1). Infinite-scroll paging returns 68 unique IDs across offset 0/50 with no duplicates and `hasMore` flipping false correctly. So the repository predicate, the alias coalescing, and the public status/expiry pinning are all behaving.

**[RETRACTED — see the corrected root cause at the top of this entry. `EnableEndpointRateLimiting: true` means per-endpoint counters, so this does not affect grid filtering. Kept for the record.]** ~~Root cause~~ — `appsettings.json` `IpRateLimiting`: `*/api/*` capped at 100 req/min per IP (also 1000/hr, 10000/day), enforced by `app.UseIpRateLimiting()` (`Program.cs:646-649`) outside Development.** Reproduced: 110 rapid requests → **103×200 + 7×429**, `Retry-After: 20`, body `{"message":"Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."}`. Note `Middleware/ApiRateLimitingMiddleware.cs:27-48` explicitly exempts `/api/certificate-tiles`, but the **AspNetCoreRateLimit `*/api/*` GeneralRule does not** — the exemption is bypassed by the other limiter. Day-bucket header read **~5000 of 10000 already consumed from this workstation's IP**, i.e. normal QA browsing is burning the quota.

**Why the page burns requests so fast:** `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view.js:727-752` fires `GET /autocomplete` on **every keystroke ≥2 chars with no debounce** — `state.debounceTimer` is declared (line 24) and `clearTimeout`'d (line 731) but **never assigned a `setTimeout`**, so the debounce is dead code. Typing a 15-char search = 14 API calls; plus one `/api/certificate-tiles` call per checkbox toggle. ~7 typed searches reaches the 100/min ceiling.

**Why it presents as "filter resets or errors" rather than an obvious rate-limit message:** `loadCertificates` (js:294-300) treats any non-`ok`, non-5xx response as terminal — **429 gets no retry and no backoff** (the retry path at 307-318 only engages for 5xx/network). On a 429 the grid **keeps the previous, stale tiles**, `#resultsCount` stays pinned at `"Loading…"` (set at js:244-247 on every fresh load and only cleared by `updateResultsCount()` on success), and the only feedback is a toast. The checkbox stays ticked and the chip stays drawn, so the user sees a filter applied but unfiltered results — reads as "the filter reset / broke."

**Two latent defects found in the same path (not the reported symptom, but real):**
1. **Tag separator mismatch.** `buildApiParams()` joins `tags`+`additional` with `'|'` (js:362-367); `CertificateTilesApiController.cs:162` splits on `','`. Selecting **2+ external tags** yields one bogus tag name, no valid match, and lines 170-173 inject the `__INVALID_TAG_FILTER__` sentinel → **guaranteed 0 results**. Currently masked because the test DB has exactly **one** external tag (`APR`); it will surface the moment a second is added. Same failure on refresh of any URL carrying `?additional=A|B`.
2. **Offset/limit truncation on infinite scroll.** Controller computes `Page = (actualOffset / actualLimit) + 1` by integer division (`CertificateTilesApiController.cs:115`), while the client advances `state.loadedCount` by **de-duplicated** count (js:270-279). Once `loadedCount` stops being an exact multiple of the 50-item batch, the offset truncates to the same page, dedup drops the whole payload, and the scroll stalls with `hasMore` permanently true. Not reachable at 68 records; reachable as the public set grows.

**Also noted:** all server-side failures on this controller return **400, not 500** (lines 220-243, 414-418, 509-524), which routes every genuine server error into the same no-retry/silent branch as the 429. And `loadFilterOptions()` (js:100-111) swallows all failures — a rate-limited `/filters` call leaves every sidebar list empty and `attachFilterEventListeners()` never binds, i.e. **the whole filter panel silently disappears**.

**Not yet done:** visual reproduction on the page itself — the `TestEnvironmentGateMiddleware` shared-password gate blocks page + static JS (`/api` is exempt, which is how the API testing above was possible). Deployed JS was therefore not diffed against the working-tree source; findings above are from source + live API behavior. No code changed pending Shawn's call on scope.

I was unaware we had any in place. And it's not past expiration date so I am not sure why it's giving me this. It was going from Draft to Republish."* Client reviewed with their team and **wants the status to be open and the complexity removed.**

**What the error actually was (not a bug):** The Status dropdown already offered all 8 statuses; the block was the **transition matrix** — a `!IsValidTransition(old, new)` guard in the Edit POST (`CertificateController.cs`) that rejected any move off the allowed-path list (Draft only → Not Paid/Confidential/Paid/Hold; Republished only reachable from Paid/Expired). Added 2026-05-19 in the DEF-203 security-hardening pass; per the 2026-07-13 client email, the *statuses* were client-defined but these *transition rules* were engineer-set and never signed off. This is the exact "Fix #2" item the email had put to the client for review — the client has now answered: remove them.

**Change made (CR-028):** Deleted the Edit-POST rejection block — any status an Analyst/Admin picks now saves. Create was already free (`Status = model.Status ?? "Draft"`, no matrix check). Narrowed the QC#188 expiry-correction auto-restore trigger to `requestedStatus == oldStatus` only, so it can't override an explicit choice now that the matrix is gone. **Kept** (confirmed with Shawn): role-based availability (External = Draft-only, data isolation — and External never reaches Edit/Create anyway) and the `CertificateStatusHistory` audit trail. **Supersedes DEF-305** (the transition-trap UX fix — no trap left). The `IsValidTransition` helper + the dead `CertificateWorkflowService.Transition*` methods left in place (minimal, reversible diff). `dotnet build` clean (0 errors). Not yet driven on localhost — server-side Edit-save change; quick authed check to follow. Regression `verify-def203.js` repurposed: section [B] now asserts the formerly-blocked hops **succeed**. Per [[feedback_data_changes_require_cr]]/[[project_qc_log_pattern]] this is a **CR, not a DEF** (changed requirement, working code). Related: [[feedback_workflow_state_count]] (8-state set is unchanged — this removes *enforcement* only).

## 2026-07-17 — CSV export shows "BurtÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s Bees" instead of "Burt's Bees" (cert 26-9648) — root cause = DATA corruption baked in before import, NOT an export bug

**Report (client, via CP):** Export database to CSV — cert **26-9648** company should be **Burt's Bees**, exports as **BurtÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s Bees**. *"Anuki please check why certain characters are creating these extra symbols."*

**Root cause (diagnosis only, no code changed):** The apostrophe in "Burt's Bees" is a **curly apostrophe ' (U+2019)**, UTF-8 bytes `E2 80 99`. `Ã¢â‚¬â„¢` is **double mojibake** — those UTF-8 bytes mis-decoded as **Windows-1252 twice**. Byte chain: correct `Burt's` → read as 1252 once → `Burtâ€™s` (single) → read as 1252 again → `BurtÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s` (double, what the client sees). **Decisive fact:** if the DB held the *correct* character, the worst any mis-set viewer could show is *single* mojibake — **double can only exist if the stored value is already corrupted.** So the value is corrupt **in the database**, and the export is faithfully re-emitting it.

**The app code is CORRECT and is exonerated:**
- Export: `CertificateService.ExportCertificatesAsync` UTF-8-encodes **once** (`CertificateService.cs:1092/1179`) → `CsvExportHelper.WithBom` only prepends a BOM, no re-encode (`CertificateController.cs:2545`). Dashboard/report exports use `ToCsvBytesWithBom` (`ExportController.cs`). All single-encode + BOM = right.
- Import reader is UTF-8 w/ BOM detection (`CertificateImportService.cs:1069`).
- Migration remediation reads source `.xlsx` via openpyxl (Unicode-safe) and writes `utf-8-sig` (`Scripts/data-ops/2026-06-22-migration-source-remediation.py`).
- **Whole-codebase sweep:** every encoding reference in all `*.cs` is UTF-8; the only "Windows-1252" strings are *comments* explaining the BOM defense. No `GetEncoding(1252)`, `Encoding.Latin1`, `Encoding.ASCII`, or `Encoding.Default` anywhere. The app **cannot** be the corruptor.

**Where the corruption actually came from:** external source-data prep before import — a UTF-8 apostrophe run through **Excel's ANSI "CSV (Comma delimited)" save** or a text editor at the wrong codepage, which decodes `E2 80 99` as Windows-1252. Double mojibake ⇒ it went through **more than one** wrong-encoding round-trip (each Excel ANSI open/save compounds it) before the value ever reached the DB. This is the established **[[feedback_data_issue_vs_defect]]** pattern (correct code + broken historical rows = data op, **no DEF row**), same family as **[[feedback_cert_number_vs_id_resolved]]**.

**Fix path (not started — awaiting Shawn):** (1) read-only sweep for all mojibake signatures (`â€™ â€œ â€ Ã© Ã¢ Ã¢â‚¬ …`) across Companies/Products/cert names to size the blast radius; (2) targeted UPDATE to restore correct characters. Test env (gccwebapp.com) but **real records → [[feedback_data_changes_require_cr]]** still applies. 100%-confirm query available: `SELECT Id, Name, CONVERT(varbinary(64), Name) FROM Companies WHERE Name LIKE '%Burt%'` to show the stored bytes directly.

**SWEEP BUILT + RUN (2026-07-17, read-only):** `Scripts/data-ops/2026-07-17-mojibake-encoding-detection-IDENTIFY.sql` — schema-wide detector; forces `COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2` (default CI_AS is accent-insensitive → `LIKE N'%Ã%'` would match every 'a'); flags lead chars `Ã`/`Â`/`â`, reports MarkerFound + Severity + UTF-16 hex. Validated on **dev DB = 0 hits, "Burt's Bees" (Id 62) stored CORRECTLY (U+2019).** Ran on **test env** (`68.71.129.120/gccwebap_certificates`): **95 rows, all QA encoding-torture fixtures** — Products.Name 47, CertificateProductIds.ProductName 43, Companies.Name 5. **Every row is a deliberately-seeded edge-case:** `Test Edge Product 00NN — Unicode Apostrophe / Smart Quotes / Emoji / French Café Crème Brûlée / German Kärcher Encoding Check`, plus companies `Kärcher`, `Gemma's Company Co.®`, `Company Symbol Test`, a >100-char test name, and a **duplicate corrupt `Burt's Bees` (Id 288, stored single-mojibake `â€™`)**. The client's cert **26-9648 is itself a test-edge cert** (product "…0049 German Kärcher Encoding Check") whose company FK points at the corrupt dup Id 288. **No generator in repo; absent from dev ⇒ loaded out-of-band directly into test env** (manual paste / ad-hoc SQL / non-app tool that mis-decoded UTF-8 as 1252). **Zero real client records affected; genuine Burt's Bees (Id 62) clean.** **Same pattern as [[feedback_cert_number_vs_id_resolved]] — the alarming thing the client saw is TEST SEED DATA, not a code bug or real-record corruption.** Why *double* mojibake when stored is *single*: the client's spreadsheet opened the CSV as Windows-1252 (BOM not honored / BOM helper maybe not yet deployed to test env), rendering stored `â€™` as `Ã¢â‚¬â„¢`. Recommendation: **no code change** (export is correct); **no real-record CR** (disposable fixtures) — either delete or re-seed the edge-case battery correctly, and tell the client 26-9648 is a test row. Full row list: session tool-result `b9i0vusea.txt`.

**RESOLVED — corrupt fixtures DELETED from test env (2026-07-19, Shawn authorized "delete the test fixtures, corrupt rows only"):** Scope confirmed 100% contained (entanglement check empty — no real cert touched). Built `Scripts/data-ops/2026-07-19-delete-corrupt-encoding-fixtures-REMEDIATE.sql` — transactional, `SET XACT_ABORT ON` + dry-run flag (`-v Commit=0/1`), an over-delete guard (aborts if any target cert isn't in the Test Edge set), needs `SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON` (CR-187 computed `NormalizedName` cols). FK map: all `Certificates` children CASCADE, so deleting a cert auto-removes its ProductIds/StatusHistory/Docs/Tags/Partners/CustomFieldValues; only `Certificates.CompanyId/ProductId` + `Products.CompanyId` are NO_ACTION (cleared in order; clean products on a corrupt company get `CompanyId=NULL` and survive). Backup of every deleted row saved to `Scripts/data-ops/_backups/2026-07-19-corrupt-encoding-fixtures/deleted-rows-backup.txt` (853 rows incl. hex). **Deleted: 5 companies (incl. dup Burt's Id 288), 47 products, 47 certs (incl. 26-9648), 752 cascaded product-IDs.** Dry run → post-delete mojibake 0/0/0 and real Burt's (Id 62) intact → committed. Independent re-run of the detection sweep = **0 rows, Section 1 & 2 empty**; kept ~130 clean Test Edge fixtures. **[[feedback_data_issue_vs_defect]] → no DEF row.** Client note drafted (26-9648 was test data; real records unaffected; export code is correct). Scripts left uncommitted per [[feedback_no_commits]].

## 2026-07-16 — Mobile login loops back to sign-in on the test env — root cause = HTTP Basic Auth gate colliding with the app's cookie login; decision pending one phone check

**Report (Shawn, mobile testers):** On the test env, signing in on a phone as **any role except public** (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) bounces straight back to the login page and never completes. *"Once in under public can log in under any other tester kind."* Desktop is unaffected.

**What I checked (live, read-only):** Drove the real browser to `https://gccwebapp.com/Account/Login` and pulled raw response headers. The whole test env sits behind an **IIS/Plesk HTTP Basic Auth gate** — `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="GCC Test Environment"` on every request (a no-credential request 401s; the browser only reaches the green login form because it already cached the gate creds). See [[project_test_env_access_gate]], [[feedback_prelaunch_test_env]].

**Leading root cause:** Basic Auth in front of a cookie-based form login is a known-bad combo on mobile. The app already emits `401` for its own logic (`Program.cs:256`, `OnRedirectToLogin`), and a non-public sign-in is a multi-step POST→302→GET chain (2FA is on by default, `Program.cs:203`; the 2FA landing bounces to Login if its TempData cookie is missing, `AccountController.cs:717-722`). Mobile browsers inconsistently re-attach the `Authorization: Basic` header across POST→redirect hops; drop it once and the app's `401` collides with the Basic realm's `401` → back to login. Browsing **public** first is plain GETs that fully prime both the gate credential and the session cookie — which is exactly why "public first, then anyone works." This **supersedes** my earlier Secure-cookie/2FA-only theory (that's a real secondary weakness, not the primary driver).

**Not yet confirmed — one 30-second phone test decides it:** when it bounces on a real phone, note which prompt reappears — the **grey native browser popup** ("GCC Test Environment") = Basic gate collision (confirmed); the **green "Welcome Back" form** = app cookie/2FA handoff instead.

**DECISION (provisional, pending the phone check):** Keep an "extra gate" on mobile, but change its *mechanism* off Basic Auth. Preferred = a **cookie-based gate page** (shared-password splash that sets a gate cookie) — preserves the current "log in twice" UX, but the second layer is a cookie mobile handles consistently, so it stops colliding with the app login. Alternatives considered: IP allowlist (silent, but bad fit for roaming cellular testers); exclude `/Account/*` from the gate (partial). Independent hardening regardless of gate choice: add `UseForwardedHeaders` + cookie `SecurePolicy=Always` so cookies get `Secure` over HTTPS (none present today; all cookies use `SameAsRequest`).

**Constraints noted:** the gate change is an **IIS/Plesk env-level** edit, not app code — needs Shawn's OK before making it. No app code changed today; this is diagnosis only. Classification (DEF vs environment issue vs CR) is Shawn's call — it's a test-env infra fault, not an app-logic defect.

**Next action:** (1) Shawn runs the one-phone prompt check; (2) if grey popup → I draft the cookie-based gate page + the `UseForwardedHeaders`/`Secure` hardening; (3) apply on Plesk and re-test on a real phone.

**IMPLEMENTED same day (in working tree, uncommitted per [[feedback_no_commits]] — pending deploy + real-phone verify):** Discovered the gate is **app middleware**, not a Plesk/IIS setting — `Middleware/TestEnvironmentGateMiddleware.cs`, enabled in `appsettings.Production.json` (the live test env), previously issuing a 401 Basic challenge. Reworked it to a **cookie gate** while keeping Basic-header acceptance:
- New `Mode` option (`Cookie` default / `Basic` = old behavior, a no-code rollback lever) + `CookieDays` (7). Added to `appsettings.json` + `appsettings.Production.json` (`Mode: Cookie`).
- **Cookie mode:** browsers with no gate cookie are **302'd to a self-contained `/__gate` password page** (inline CSS, mobile viewport, 16px fields, GCC gradient) instead of getting a 401 Basic popup. Correct password → data-protected `GCC.TestGate` cookie, **`SameSite=Lax` + `HttpOnly` + `Secure=IsHttps`**, then redirect to the preserved `returnUrl`. Lax (not Strict) so it survives arrival from an external link and rides the app's login POST→redirect chain — which is the actual mobile fix.
- **Compat preserved:** a valid **Basic header still passes** (both modes), so the ~30 Playwright smoke/deploy-gate scripts that send `httpCredentials: gcc/Cert-Test-Access-2026!` keep working untouched. `/api/*`, robots, favicon, and SEO-verification exemptions unchanged. `ShowBanner` (read in `_Layout.cshtml`) left alone.
- CSRF guard on the gate POST (data-protected `formToken`, 30-min TTL); open-redirect guard on `returnUrl`; constant-time password compare retained.
- **Verified:** clean build (0 errors). Localhost curl matrix 8/8 — no-cookie→gate 302, gate page renders w/ token, correct pw→Lax+HttpOnly cookie+302, cookie'd request passes, wrong pw→401 no cookie, **Basic header→200 (script compat)**, `/api`→its own 401 (not a gate redirect), missing token→400. Browser screenshot of `/__gate` at 378px confirms clean mobile render. Files: `Middleware/TestEnvironmentGateMiddleware.cs`, `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.Production.json`. **Not yet done:** DEF/CR classification (Shawn's call), the separate `UseForwardedHeaders`+`Secure` app-cookie hardening (still worth doing), deploy, and the real-phone re-test. Note: the one-phone confirmation was **not** run before building — Shawn directed "make the fix"; the change is strictly better than Basic even if the app-cookie layer is also implicated, but confirm on a phone post-deploy.

**Secure-cookie hardening added same day — but NOT `UseForwardedHeaders` (deliberately).** Checked `web.config`: the app is **IIS `hostingModel="inprocess"`** (AspNetCoreModuleV2) with an IIS HTTP→HTTPS redirect rule. In-process hosting surfaces the real client scheme, so `Request.IsHttps`/`Scheme` are already correct — `UseForwardedHeaders` is a **no-op here** (it's for out-of-process/Kestrel-behind-proxy, e.g. the Docker path), and forcing it to "work" by clearing KnownProxies would let clients spoof `X-Forwarded-For` and undermine `UseIpRateLimiting`. So the original "cookies emitted without Secure over HTTPS" worry doesn't hold on this deployment; skipped FH. Instead did the hardening those three standing `// TODO: change back to CookieSecurePolicy.Always` comments actually asked for: added `var cookieSecurePolicy = IsDevelopment() ? SameAsRequest : Always` (`Program.cs` after builder create) and applied it to the **session, auth (`GCC.Auth`), and antiforgery** cookies — so Test/Prod always set `Secure`, Development (plain-HTTP localhost) stays `SameAsRequest` so local login still works. Build clean (0 errors); Development flow unchanged (already-verified gate test uses the SameAsRequest branch). The `Secure`-over-HTTPS behavior gets confirmed on the real test env during the post-deploy phone check. If the app ever moves to the Docker/out-of-process path, THEN add `UseForwardedHeaders` (with `ForwardedProto` + explicit KnownProxies) — noted for that future. File: `Program.cs`.

## 2026-06-29 — Certificate tile compaction: removed legacy whitespace, made the blue header a consistent height, hardened it across all 3 views + responsive breakpoints

Client ask: *"reduce padding for the certificate tile."* What looked like a padding tweak turned into unwinding a set of **legacy fixed dimensions in `main.css` (under `body.theme-option4`) that were silently overriding the earlier QC #199 shrink-to-content work** via higher CSS specificity — so that work had been authored but had no visual effect. The real whitespace drivers were: `.card-header { min-height: 220px }` (240px mobile), `.product-name { height: 170px }` (a fixed 3-line reservation), `.card-body { min-height: 200px }`, and `.certificates-grid { align-items: stretch }`. All fixes were scoped to `body.theme-option4 .certificate-card …` in `wwwroot/css/certificatetileview.css` so the global Bootstrap `.card-header`/`.card-body` (modals, single-cert detail view) stay untouched.

**What shipped (working tree, uncommitted per [[feedback_no_commits]]):**
- **Header → consistent fixed height.** First attempt (min-height floor) was reverted by the client because short-company tiles shrank while long-company tiles grew → *inconsistent* blue headers. Re-did it as a true fixed height sized to the 3-line-company worst case: **public 165px** (down from 220/240). The company name is already clamped to 3 lines, so the worst case is bounded; trimmed `.company-name` (margin-top 10→4, padding 8→4) and `.header-row` (margin-bottom 4→2) to fit a tighter 165 while keeping ~14px green-wave clearance. Client kept the 3-line capability.
- **Body vertical spacing** trimmed (`.card-body`, `.certificate-details`, `.certificate-period`, `.certificate-location` vertical margins/padding; `product-name` height→auto; `card-body justify-content: space-between`→`flex-start` so the certification period sits directly under the product name). Card height dropped ~615px → ~371px on the public view.
- **`.card-actions` bottom padding** restored to 10px (had been over-trimmed to 2px — icons were flush to the card edge).

**The recurring internal/external scoping trap ([[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]], same pattern, CSS edition):** the public fix would have **clipped** the external and internal views, which carry a 4-row header (category/cert#, company, **Status**, optional **Partner**) the public 2-row header doesn't. Caught by checking the adjacent views before calling it done. Resolved by scoping public's 165px to `:not(.internal-card)`, giving **internal** its own `.internal-card` rule and **external** its own rule in `wwwroot/css/pages/certificate-tile-external.css` (the external-only stylesheet) — both a consistent **200px** sized for *their* worst case (3-line company + Status + Partner ≈ 196px). Internal/external also got the compact 6px header padding.

**Responsive (client explicitly asked to check mobile + tablet):** at ≤768px `main.css` stacks the `header-row` into a column, dropping the cert# pill onto its own line *and* pushing the header tall enough that the company/Status row overlapped the green wave. Fixed by (a) keeping the header-row **inline** at the breakpoint (cert# stays top-right) and (b) switching the header to **auto-height + bottom padding** so it grows to fit however many lines the (unclamped) category wraps to and always clears the wave. Then **extended the safety to ≤1024px** so the whole tablet range adapts; true desktop (>1024px) keeps the fixed *consistent* heights, tablet/mobile get *ragged-but-never-overlapping* headers.

**Verified on localhost across the matrix:** desktop >1024 (uniform 165/200, clean), tablet 900px (auto, 22px clearance, cert# inline), mobile 407px (clean on **public, internal, external**) — zero clipping/overlap everywhere, worst case being the seeded "Testing Very Very Long Company…" + "PRODUCT OPTIMIZATION: CARBON FOOTPRINT REDUCTION" 3-line-category card. This was a client-driven UI refinement, not a defect (no DEF row; embedded bugs found along the way — the mobile wave-overlap and cert#-stacking — were fixed in the same pass). Files: `wwwroot/css/certificatetileview.css`, `wwwroot/css/pages/certificate-tile-external.css`.

**Follow-up same day — breakpoint consistency pass.** Client noticed the vertical spacing wasn't consistent across breakpoints. Audit (CSS + live measure at 900px) showed body spacing is consistent *view-to-view* (it all lives in the shared `certificatetileview.css`; `certificate-tile-internal.css` has zero body rules, external's only adds header height) and consistent desktop↔tablet, but **diverged at ≤768px** from a legacy `main.css` mobile block. Fixed two leaks by adding `min-height:0` to `.certificate-details` and `margin-top:auto` to `.card-actions` on the existing `.certificate-card`-scoped base rules (specificity 0,3,1 beats main.css's mobile 0,2,1, so they win at every width). Discovered the `.certificate-tags` R143 `margin-bottom:18px` mobile override has been **dead since QC #199** — shadowed by the higher-specificity `.card-body > *:last-child { margin-bottom:4px }` — so tag margin was already consistent at 4px (kept R143's `padding-bottom:8px`, the only still-live piece, per client's "keep it" call). #3 (card-actions side padding 15px vs 6px, horizontal) left untouched.

**Follow-up same day — internal Partner row overlap (26-0161, "Partner: Wayfair").** Client spotted the Partner row cut by the green wave on the internal worst-case card. Root cause was a **CSS source-order bug in my own responsive work**: the `@media (max-width:1024px)` internal auto-height rule had been placed *above* the internal desktop fixed-height rule (`height:200px`), and with equal specificity the later (desktop) rule won at every width — so internal **never actually got auto-height**; it stayed locked at 200px and the 4-row worst case overlapped the wave at narrow widths (the earlier 407px pass was luck-of-the-loaded-cards). Public worked (its desktop rule sits before the media block) and external worked (its mobile rule is after its desktop rule in the external file) — internal was the lone asymmetry. Fix: moved the internal desktop rule *above* the media block. Verified at 375px — header now auto-grows 200→235px, `padding-bottom:22px` applies, Partner row clears the wave by 22px (was 6px), `anyOverlap:false` across all internal cards. Reinforces that responsive overrides must sit **after** the base rules they override. File: `wwwroot/css/certificatetileview.css`.

## 2026-06-26 — DEF-299 FIXED: external table view column-sort fired descending on first click (External Tag)

Shawn relayed a user report: *"external tag sorting on the certificate view table is not sorting correctly… they want the first tag to sort ascending vs descending."* Traced to `wwwroot/js/certificate-tile-view-external.js::setupTableColumnSort`, which seeded the sort direction as `header.dataset.sortDir || 'asc'` then **immediately flipped it** — so a never-clicked header resolved to `'asc'` and flipped to `'desc'`, making the *first* click descending. The bug was global to every sortable header in the external table view, but surfaced on the **External Tag** column. The **internal** view already had the correct logic (`!currentDir ? 'asc' : …`) plus a sibling-column reset — the external view was just out of sync (the recurring internal/external [[feedback_scoping_check_adjacent_endpoints]] pattern). Fix: aligned the external handler with the internal one — first click → ascending (A-Z, ▲), second click on the same column → descending (Z-A, ▼), clicking a different column clears the others so only one active direction exists. The existing `reverseSortMap` (`ext-tag → ext-tag-za`) already supplied the descending sort key, so no API change. Logged as [[DEF-299]]. Pending next deploy.

Shawn's ask: *"confirm the Amazon API has not changed when Amazon makes a call."* Built `Scripts/smoke-prod/amazon-contract-diff.js` — it pulls each Amazon-facing response live (as Amazon does: `X-API-Key`, cookie-free) and diffs its **structure** (every field path, array-vs-object nesting, leaf type; data **values** ignored since the dataset varies) against the saved pre-CR-171 baseline samples in `docs/tracking/api-samples/`. Null leaves are treated as wildcards so a nullable field doesn't false-diff.

- **GS1 list** `/api/v1/certificates/gs1` vs `2026-04-30_amazon_gs1.json` — identical (`@context`/`$schema`/`type:CertificationReport`/`products[].additionalTradeItemId[]`/`certificationInfo{…targetCountries[]…amazonCode,pathway}`).
- **GS1 single** `/api/v1/certificates/gs1/26-0146` vs `2026-04-30_amazon_gs1_single.json` — identical.
- **Standard list** `/api/v1/certificates?includeProductIds=true` vs `2026-04-24_amazon_standard.json` — identical (`certificateNumber,status,issueDate,expirationDate,certificationCountries,partner,certificationResults,pathway,company,productName,certificationType,amazonCode,issuer,productIds[]{type,value,status,partner,productName,productSku},pdfDownloadUrl`).

Zero fields added, removed, renamed, or retyped. This is the mechanical proof of [[feedback_amazon_api_immutable]]: everything since April — CR-171 (multi-partner + isolation), CR-186/187, and today's DEF-269 — changed only **which** partner value is returned (caller-scoped) and the `/search` param nullability, **never the shape Amazon parses.** Reusable: `node Scripts/smoke-prod/amazon-contract-diff.js` (BASE_URL override; defaults localhost:5101). Note: run against the same seed dataset the baselines were captured from (the 6 Amazon certs incl. 26-0146); a future contract check after a schema change should re-diff against these same files.

## 2026-06-22 — Amazon Partner API full localhost functional test: 45/45 green on the data sent to Amazon; 2 minor non-Amazon findings logged (DEF-269/270)

Shawn's ask: *"test localhost all the API functionality and test data that would be sent to Amazon."* Built a self-contained partner-API harness (`Scripts/smoke-prod/amazon-partner-api-local.js`) that drives **every partner-facing endpoint exactly as Amazon does** — `X-API-Key: gcc_partner_…` header, **no session cookie** — and validates each response against the Amazon Developer Guide contract. Setup is self-contained: admin-cookie login → discover the Amazon partner → generate a fresh partner key → exercise the v1 endpoints with that key from a **cookie-free** request context.

**Key environmental gotcha (worth remembering):** the partner middleware (`PartnerApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware`) **skips API-key auth when a cookie session already exists** (cookie takes precedence), and the v1 controller is `[Authorize(AuthenticationSchemes="ApiKey")]`. So a request carrying *both* the admin cookie **and** a valid `X-API-Key` 401s. Real Amazon traffic is cookie-free; the test must isolate the partner calls in their own cookie-less context (Playwright `request.newContext()`), or every partner endpoint falsely 401s. First two test iterations failed on exactly this until the contexts were split.

**Result: 45 passed / 0 failed / 1 expected warning.** Endpoints verified 200 + contract-clean: `GET /certificates?includeProductIds=true`, `GET /certificates`, **`GET /certificates/gs1` (the GS1 JSON-LD Amazon actually ingests)**, `GET /certificates/gs1/{n}`, `GET /certificates/number/{n}`, `GET /certificates/expiring`, `GET /certificates/search`, `GET /certificates/search/productid?type=ASIN` (found the cert by ASIN). Contract guarantees confirmed on the data sent to Amazon: **status always `Active`** (no internal lifecycle leak), **`certificationCountries`/`targetCountries` always `"All"`**, **zero co-partner leakage** (CR-171 — `Novi`/`Wayfair`/`Other` never appear in any Amazon response), and the GS1 shape (`@context`, `$schema`, `type: CertificationReport`, `amazonCode`, `pathway`, `certificationResults` as a %). Auth guards: missing key → 401, invalid key → 401. Dated GS1 sample receipt written to `docs/tracking/api-samples/2026-06-22_amazon_gs1_localtest.json`.

**Two minor findings (NEITHER affects the Amazon GS1 data path) — logged per Shawn's request:**
- **[[DEF-270]]** — `GET /api/v1/certificates/{id}/download` has no PDF-generation fallback: returns 404 *"PDF generation not yet implemented"* when no physical PDF exists. Path resolution is correct (App_Data-first, DEF-208-aware — not the [[DEF-264]] MVC bug); the gap is the unimplemented generate-fallback, which **contradicts the Swagger doc** that promises a generated PDF. Locally every seeded cert lacks a file so it 404s 100%; on prod it only bites file-less certs. The `pdfDownloadUrl` field itself is emitted correctly. Triage: implement the fallback (option A) or fix the doc (option B).
- **[[DEF-269]]** — `GET /api/v1/certificates/search`: `term` and `status` are non-nullable params → implicitly `[Required]`, so empty `term` 400s; and `status` does a literal match against the **internal** status, so a partner passing `status=Active` matches 0 rows (certs are stored as "Client Approved - Paid" etc., reported as "Active" only in output). Recommend `string? term`/`string? status` + mapping `Active`→public-status set for partner callers. Amazon uses GS1, not `/search`.

Both filed **OPEN/triage, no code change** (per [[feedback_qc_review_no_changes]] — this was a test task, not a fix request). The Amazon contract question is independently answered **YES — the data sent to Amazon is correct and isolation-clean.** New artifact: `Scripts/smoke-prod/amazon-partner-api-local.js` (reusable; `BASE_URL` env override, defaults to localhost:5101).

## 2026-06-01 — E2E Tier 1 smoke fan-out EXECUTED: 10/10 views green (0 FAIL)

Ran the full Tier 1 suite on localhost:5101 (`node Scripts/smoke-prod/_views/run-all.js`) — the run that follows the Day 2 build entry below. All 10 critical views pass with **0 FAIL** — ~694 assertions across 4 roles × 3 viewports. Per-view: home 104P · login 28P · cert-tile-public 124P · cert-tile-external 96P · cert-tile-internal 62P · cert-create 80P · cert-edit 62P/6W · dashboard 58P · admin-user-mgmt 40P · admin-tags 40P. Negative-path access (Public/External/Analyst hitting views above their level) all returned the expected 401/403 → counted as PASS. Roll-up artifact: `Scripts/smoke-prod/_results/summary-{stamp}.json`.

**Stable finding (data, not code):** cert **26-0025** (company *HID Global*) points at product id 6 (*"Bottles"*), which is NOT in HID Global's product list — so its Edit page renders a blank Product Name. Flagged **WARN = data-ops**, not a DEF, per [[feedback_data_issue_vs_defect]]. Almost certainly DEF-231 fallout → independently corroborates the **CR-019** cleanup. The cert-edit smoke distinguishes this from a true DEF-225 re-selection regression (saved product present-in-options-but-not-selected → it would FAIL).

**Important nuance on "10/10 green":** the **per-view** result is conclusively green — each of the 10 views was run and passed 0-FAIL (694P/0F/6W total; every view individually confirmed, admin-tags re-verified standalone at 40P/0F). But the **single-process orchestrated `run-all`** is flaky for an environmental reason, not a view defect: the local **dev server reliably becomes unresponsive / exits near the tail of a sustained ~6-min full run** (views 1-9 pass, then the next view's cells all fail with `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` / `page.goto` timeout). Diagnosed over several runs — contributors: (1) **zombie process pileup** — repeated `dotnet run`/stopped-`run-all` invocations left up to 5 concurrent node runners + multiple dotnet listeners hammering one server and fighting over port 5101 (`AddressInUseException`); cleared with `Get-Process dotnet,node,chrome | Stop-Process`. (2) Even with a single clean server + one runner, the server still tips over near the end of the run — likely cumulative overhead from the verbose per-request `RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware` + the global-locked, unbounded `_securityEvents` list in `SecurityMonitoringService` (which also logs a noisy but harmless "Rapid request pattern" SuspiciousActivity warning for the smoke's burst traffic — it only logs, does not block). **Resolution:** added an opt-in **batch-with-restart mode** to `run-all.js` (`SMOKE_BATCH_RESTART=1`, `SMOKE_BATCH_SIZE` default 5) — the script owns the server lifecycle and starts a fresh `dotnet run` before each batch, so no batch accumulates enough sustained load to fell the server. Ran it end-to-end: **694 PASS / 0 FAIL / 6 WARN → STATUS GREEN ✅** (2 batches of 5, zero retries; admin-tags, which died at view 10 in single-run, passed 40P/0F on the fresh batch-2 server). The 6 WARN are the cert-26-0025 data anomaly (CR-019) — the only non-PASS. Recommended command going forward: `SMOKE_BATCH_RESTART=1 node Scripts/smoke-prod/_views/run-all.js`. Harness also hardened with warm-up, 60s nav timeout (`SMOKE_NAV_TIMEOUT`), inter-view cooldown (`SMOKE_COOLDOWN_MS`), and a single auto-retry of any RED view. Remaining real code-side follow-up: DEF-234 (cold-start tile-API perf).

**Two infra bugs found + fixed during the run:** (1) the access-check heuristic misread the login page's own legitimate 200 as a 401 — fixed by skipping the redirect heuristic when the requested URL is itself an `/Account/*` page; (2) the dev server stalls ~20-25s on a cold first hit (heavy stats pages + per-minute expiration sweep), tripping Playwright's 30s nav default — an early rollup went RED on 6 such `page.goto` timeouts that all passed clean on re-run once warm. Fixed: 60s nav timeout (`SMOKE_NAV_TIMEOUT`) + server warm-up in `run-all.js`. Internal QA tooling — no DEF, no client-facing change.

## 2026-05-21 — DEF-107 root cause fully traced: web.config + middleware double-injection (fix landed)

Today's grouped sweep flagged `Permissions-Policy` header still duplicated on prod despite DEF-107 being marked "Fixed locally". Investigated and found the original 5/1 fix was correct but **incomplete** — it removed the legacy `Feature-Policy` header from the middleware, but the actual prod-side duplication was a separate issue.

**Root cause (the bigger picture):** Security headers were being added at TWO layers:
- **IIS** via `web.config` `<httpProtocol><customHeaders>` — X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy
- **ASP.NET Core middleware** (`SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs`) — same set + a few extras

`response.Headers.Append(...)` in middleware adds a SECOND value on a header IIS already set. The browser sees BOTH. Some values disagreed (X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN in IIS vs DENY in middleware; X-XSS-Protection: "1; mode=block" vs "0"; CSP differed too). On Kestrel (dev) this never reproduced because Kestrel doesn't honor web.config — only IIS does.

**Fix:** Removed the entire `<httpProtocol>` block from `web.config:22-36` and replaced with an explanatory comment. Middleware is now the single source of truth — environment-aware (different CSP dev vs prod), applies before `UseStaticFiles` so static assets get the same headers, and works identically across Kestrel and IIS.

**Verified on localhost:** `HEAD /` returns exactly 1 of each header. Single Permissions-Policy, single X-Frame-Options (DENY), single CSP (the comprehensive middleware-built one). Localhost was always clean — the test confirms middleware still emits everything correctly. Final prod verification deferred to next deploy.

**DEF-107 register entry rewritten** to capture the full scope of the bug (not just Feature-Policy → Permissions-Policy, but every duplicated header), the 2026-05-21 re-discovery via status-sync sweep, the consolidated fix, and a cross-ref to DEF-135 / DEF-108 (CSP maintenance now happens in one place).

**Why the original 5/1 entry was misleading:** It said "Fixed locally — pending deploy" with the Feature-Policy comment, but the wider IIS-layer duplication was never caught. Anyone reading the entry between 5/1 and 5/21 reasonably assumed it was closed. The status-sync sweep saved the day — without it, this would have shipped to production launch with conflicting X-Frame-Options values and a duplicate CSP.

Cross-cutting lesson worth flagging for similar future cases: **when a header/policy is configured in multiple layers (IIS web.config, middleware, response decorator), every layer's output stacks.** Don't trust "Fixed locally" status without checking the deployed HTTP response for the count of each header.

## 2026-05-21 — DEF-215: Password reset link silently fails — double URL-decode corrupted base64 tokens

Shawn ran a local password-reset against his own account, received the email, clicked the link, and landed on the reset page already showing **"This password reset link is invalid or has expired. Please request a new one."** before he could enter a new password.

**Root cause:** `Controllers/AccountController.cs` was calling `WebUtility.UrlDecode` on the inbound `token` parameter in both the GET (`:504`) and POST (`:550`) handlers. ASP.NET Core's model binder already URL-decodes query-string parameters and form bodies, so the second decode flipped any `+` (a valid base64 alphabet char) into a space — and base64 SHA-256 hash compare fails on a single-character mismatch. Roughly 75% of issued tokens contain at least one `+` or `/`, so most reset links would fail; the rare success cases were tokens that happened to use only `A-Z a-z 0-9 = `. End-to-end success was even lower because the hidden-field round-trip on submit hit the same bug a second time.

**Fix:** dropped the redundant `WebUtility.UrlDecode` call in both handlers (lines 504-506 and 550-552), hash `token` / `model.Token` directly. Two-line removal. Build is clean — only obstacle to local verification was the dev exe being held by the running app process.

Defect filed as **DEF-215** in `docs/tracking/defect-register.md`. Test plan covers happy path, round-trip, and three negative paths (expired / wrong-token / used-token) to confirm those branches are unchanged. Follow-up: integration test that drives the full forgot-password → click-link → submit loop end-to-end (no existing test exercised the URL round-trip, which is why the bug survived).

This needs to ship on the next deploy ahead of the production cutover — once Basic Auth comes down at launch, the password-reset flow becomes the only recovery path, and a 25%-success-rate recovery flow would create a support fire-drill on day one.

## 2026-05-21 — Auth hardening (DEF-209 + DEF-210) verified end-to-end: email-enumeration closed + brute-force lockout proven

Critical pre-launch security work. Internal QA flagged 5/19 that login error messages disclosed valid emails ("User not found" vs "Invalid password") and that the login endpoint had no rate-limit or lockout. Fixed under DEF-209 (generic message + async ForgotPassword) and DEF-210 (5-attempt → 15-min per-account lockout). Both deployed 5/20.

**Localhost full destructive matrix** (`qc209-210-auth-hardening.js`): 9 / 9 PASS.

DEF-209 evidence:
- 3 failure modes (nonexistent / valid-email-wrong-pw / malformed) all return identical `"Invalid email or password."` — no leakage.
- ForgotPassword timing collapsed from a pre-fix ~3000ms vs ~30ms (100× side-channel) to **69ms vs 17ms (52ms delta)** post-fix. Synchronous SMTP replaced with fire-and-forget `Task.Run`.

DEF-210 evidence (full lockout cycle on `jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com`):
- 5 wrong attempts → `FailedLoginAttempts` 0→5, `LockedUntil` set to `2026-05-21 22:11:53`
- 6th attempt with **CORRECT** password rejected (proves locked-state short-circuit BEFORE password verify, important so locked-account probes can't re-extend the lockout)
- Force-expire LockedUntil → correct password returns HTTP 302 (successful redirect)
- Successful login resets counter 5→0 and clears LockedUntil
- Test user state restored at end (counter=0, LockedUntil=NULL)

**gccwebapp.com read-only deploy probe**: 3 / 3 PASS.
- Live login error messages identical across nonexistent + malformed email
- Live ForgotPassword both calls <500ms (347ms + 247ms, delta 100ms) — confirms async send pattern deployed
- Lockout NOT exercised on prod per the `[Data Changes Require CR]` rule. Shared code path with DEF-209 plus localhost full-cycle proof.

Two small fixes to the harness worth noting: (a) the dev DB's analyst seed email is `jane.analyst@anukiconsulting.com` (NOT `analyst@test-gcc.local` from old `SeedData.cs`); (b) ForgotPassword needs a warm-up call before timing measurement to remove DB connection + anti-forgery cookie setup overhead.

## 2026-05-19 — DEF-200 / QC #180: Dashboard tile↔export divergence (mass alignment + one wrong-column bug)

Client raised QC #180 on 5/11 — *"Certs Expired Last Month is not using right data … Anuki needs to do that"* (the count audit). Audited every dashboard tile against its export and found the gap was broader than the headline: every "Active …" card and the "Expired Last Month" card disagreed with their downloads. Three root causes:

1. **Wrong column.** `Controllers/DashboardController.cs:certs-expired-last-month` called `GetCertificatesByDateRangeAsync(start, end)`, which filters on `EffectiveDate`. So "Expired Last Month" returned certs that became *effective* last month. Plus no status filter → Drafts with stale ExpirationDates leaked through.
2. **Missing aggregation case.** `GenerateAggregatedStatCsv` had cases for categories/types/subcategories/companies but not Products, so `products-with-active-certs` exported per-cert rows (22) instead of distinct products (10).
3. **Tile counted future-dated certs.** `Repositories/CertificateRepository.cs:580-582` had `EffectiveDate >= startOfYear` with no upper bound, so a `2027-07-08` future cert was counted in "Published This Year" tile (16) but excluded from export (15).

Fix introduced `CertificateStatusHelper.EverPublishedStatuses` (DashboardStatuses ∪ {Expired, ExpiredNoAnnualVerification}) as a named constant for the "ever-published" set used by ExpiredLastMonth. New `GetCertificatesByExpirationDateRangeAsync` helper for the right column. DashboardController switched to both. Products added to aggregation. PublishedThisYear capped at today. Parallel `/Export/DownloadStat` aligned defensively.

Verified on dev: all 12 dashboard cards now have tile=export. Probe for ExpiredLastMonth: temporarily set cert 27 ExpirationDate to 2026-04-15; background expiration service auto-flipped Draft→Expired (correct); tile and export both returned exactly 1 row matching that cert; fixture reverted.

Time-trap worth remembering: `wwwroot/js/dashboard.js` runs a 1.5s count-up animation on every stat-value. Playwright `waitUntil:'networkidle'` fires before that completes, so initial verification captured mid-counter values (e.g. 7 instead of 22) and sent me down a phantom rabbit hole investigating why "Statistics['Active']" was returning 7 — it wasn't, the test snapshot just caught the animation mid-roll. Any future automated dashboard test needs `await page.waitForTimeout(2000)` after `goto`.

Build: 0 errors, 51 pre-existing warnings (unchanged). Files: `Models/CertificateStatus.cs`, `Repositories/ICertificateRepository.cs`, `Repositories/CertificateRepository.cs`, `Controllers/DashboardController.cs`, `Controllers/ExportController.cs`. Tracking: `docs/tracking/defect-register.md` (DEF-200), `docs/tracking/shipped-2026-05.md`.

## 2026-05-18 — DEF-197 (no QC ref): Product Types Usage column overcounted when entities set multiple FK levels

Found during local smoke test of [[DEF-196]]. The new "Usage (Products / Certs)" column rolled up parent totals as `direct + Σ(children)`. The Certificates table allows a single row to set `ProductCategoryId` + `ProductTypeId` + `ProductSubcategoryId` simultaneously (1 of 43 dev certs does; 1 of 305 dev products does the same on the product side), so each such entity was counted at every level it set, then summed again at the grandparent.

Dev DB: Chemicals category showed `3 / 28` (page) vs `2 / 26` (truth — distinct certs/products in the subtree). Type 4 showed `2 / 2` vs `1 / 1`. Leaf subcategories were always correct. Worst-case overcount for an entity tagged at all N levels is N*(N-1)/2 extra at the root.

Fix in `Services/AdminService.cs:GetProductTypesAsync`: replaced integer-sum rollup with `HashSet<int>` unions per node, count `.Count` once at the end. UnionWith dedupes the multi-FK case naturally. Smoke re-run confirmed the page now matches SQL ground truth at every node. No data migration, no schema change, no UI change — same template renders, just with correct numbers.

Build: 0 errors, 51 pre-existing warnings (unchanged). Files: `Services/AdminService.cs`. Tracking: `docs/tracking/defect-register.md` (DEF-197), `docs/tracking/shipped-2026-05.md`.

Lesson worth keeping: `direct + Σ(children)` only works when each entity is referenced at exactly one level of a tree. As soon as the schema allows multi-level FK tagging, the rollup must dedupe on entity ID, not on count. Same shape as `[[feedback_ef_includes_with_projection]]` — counting when you should be distinct.

## 2026-05-15 — DEF-196 / QC #170: Admin → Product Types delete blocked by certs, but count column hid them

Carly's QC #170 (5/1, re-raised 5/15): she couldn't delete her "Carly Test" product type. Tree-view "Products" column showed 0 but every delete attempt returned the generic "An error occurred while deleting. Please try again." Filtering the cert list by "Carly Test" showed certs were actually using it — the admin page was lying about what was deletable.

Three layered bugs on the same path in `Services/AdminService.cs`: (1) `GetProductTypesAsync` populated `ProductCount` from `ProductType.Products` only — the EF navigation only sees `Products.ProductTypeId`, not Products linked via `ProductSubcategoryId`, and no Certificate FK at all. (2) `DeleteProductTypeAsync` pre-check used the same Products-only navigation, so it passed silently when only certs referenced the type. (3) `_context.SaveChangesAsync()` then hit the SQL Server FK Restrict on `Certificates.ProductTypeId`/`ProductSubcategoryId`/`ProductCategoryId` and got swallowed by the broad `catch (Exception)`. Same chain existed in `DeleteProductCategoryAsync`.

Fix: `GetProductTypesAsync` now reads `Certificates.ProductCategoryId/ProductTypeId/ProductSubcategoryId` and `Products.ProductSubcategoryId` upfront, populates a new `CertificateCount` field per node, and corrects Level-2 product counts. Delete methods now run explicit cert pre-checks (`ProductTypeId == id || ProductSubcategoryId == id` for types; `ProductCategoryId == id` for categories) with messages naming the count and the right noun ("subcategory" vs "type" per entity Level). A `DbUpdateException` catch sits above the generic handler as final fallback. UI: column header renamed to "Usage (Products / Certs)" with tooltip; node cells render `${productCount} / ${certificateCount}`. Table view splits into two columns. CSV exports gain a `Certificate Count` column.

Verified on local dev DB: GET `/Admin/GetProductTypes` returns both counts matching direct SQL queries. PET (subcategory with 1 cert via SubcategoryId) → "Cannot delete: 1 certificate(s) use this subcategory. Edit those certificates to use a different subcategory first, then try again." LLDPE (subcategory with 1 product via SubcategoryId — previously hidden) → "Cannot delete: 1 product(s) are assigned to this item. Please reassign them first." Plastics (has 6 subcategories) → existing children check fires first, unchanged. Build: 0 errors, 53 pre-existing warnings.

Cert Edit dropdown side-complaint is the Category→Type cascade working as designed — no code change. Workaround: change Category first to unlock the Type dropdown with non-test options. If client keeps hitting it, add a UX hint under the Type dropdown.

Files: `Services/AdminService.cs`, `Models/AdminModels.cs`, `Views/Admin/ProductTypes.cshtml`, `wwwroot/js/product-types.js`. Tracking: `docs/tracking/defect-register.md` (DEF-196), `docs/tracking/shipped-2026-05.md`.

## 2026-05-12 — Product ID Import: partial-select with a no-change row → "Import failed"

URL: `http://localhost:5101/Certificate/Edit/26-0023`. Shawn observed that selecting a subset of rows in the Import Preview without enabling Replace-all caused the import to fail.

Reproduced locally with Playwright on cert `26-0023`: upload a one-row CSV whose `Type,Product ID` already exist on the cert with identical other fields → preview classifies it as `status='unchanged', action='skip', selected=false`. User manually checks the row → JS includes it in `bulkRows` because the filter was `r.action !== 'update'`. Server rejects on the duplicate check with `"Product ID already exists on this certificate"`. Toast: `Import failed: ASIN:B08N5W0001 - Product ID already exists on this certificate`.

Root cause: `applyImport()` in `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js` partitioned `selectedRows` using a `!== 'update'` filter, which let `'skip'` rows reach the bulk endpoint as create attempts. They should have been treated as no-ops in non-overwrite mode.

Fix: changed the bulk filter to `r.action === 'create'`, added a `skippedExisting` partition, and updated the success-message branch so a skip-only selection ends with `"X row(s) already on this certificate — nothing to change"` instead of the generic failure. Mixed selections that include skips append `"; X already on file"` to the success message. Replace-all behavior unchanged. Tracked as DEF-191.

Verified by re-running the four-scenario repro against localhost — all four end in a success toast that accurately describes the outcome.

File: `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js`.

## 2026-05-11 — DEF-167 implemented: Level-1-only cert-type filter dropdown across all three tile-view controllers

Shawn's direction was Level 1 only in the dropdown, fix the data — no parent-rollup logic.

Dev DB audit first: 41 certs, all tagged at Level 1, 0 at Level 2. `CertificateCertificationTypeSubcategories` join table empty. Dev needs no data remediation. The Level-2-tagged certs the client saw are on prod (gccwebapp.com).

Code change: replaced the 18-line `allCertTypes` query + in-memory parent/child flatten loop with a single Level-1-only LINQ query in **three controllers** (turned out to be three, not two — public, internal, external all carry the same pattern):
- `Controllers/Api/CertificateTilesApiController.cs` — public, `/api/certificate-tiles` (the bug the client actually saw)
- `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileInternalApiController.cs` — admin/internal, `/api/certificate-tiles-internal` (client said "login view is fine" — parity-only fix)
- `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileExternalApiController.cs` — external-user, `/api/CertificateTileExternal` (also was missing the `IsActive` guard)

New query in all three:
```csharp
var hierarchicalCertTypes = await _context.CertificationTypes
    .Where(ct => ct.IsActive && ct.ParentId == null && certTypeIds.Contains(ct.Id))
    .OrderBy(ct => ct.SortOrder)
    .Select(ct => new { name = ct.Name, level = ct.Level })
    .ToListAsync();
```
JSON output shape unchanged (`[{name, level}, ...]`); JS consumers untouched.

Local verification: `GET /api/certificate-tiles/filters` returned 4 entries, all `level: 1`. Filter by `?certType=Recycled%20Content` returned 16 certs, all `Recycled Content`. Pre-fix would have included CSF subcategories (and on prod, all 30 of them as separate filter rows).

Wrote `Database_Scripts/20260511_DEF167_AuditL2TaggedCerts.sql` with two parts:
1. Audit SELECT (safe to run anytime) — lists every Level-2-tagged cert with its proposed parent.
2. Remediation block (commented-out, CR-gated) — repoints CertificationTypeId to the parent Level-1, preserves the original Level-2 reference in `CertificateCertificationTypeSubcategories`.

**Pre-deploy gate:** before shipping the code, run the audit query against prod. Any row count > 0 means those certs will silently disappear from filter selection until the remediation block runs. Per `feedback_data_changes_require_cr.md`, the UPDATE block needs a CR with row count attached before it can run on prod. Either submit the CR + run together, or warn the client that those Level-2-tagged certs will be temporarily unfilterable post-deploy.

Files changed: 3 controllers, 1 new SQL script. Build clean (0 errors, 51 pre-existing warnings).

## 2026-05-10 — QC #169 / DEF-167 scoped: public cert-tile filter renders subcategories + missing IsActive guard + no parent-rollup on filter selection

Client reported (QC #169, 4/30/26) that the public Certificate Tile View's "Certification Type" filter pane shows CSF subcategories as their own checkboxes ("WHICH IS WRONG"), shows what appears to be all cert types, and that selecting a parent like CSF doesn't surface certs tagged with a child subcategory like Recycled Content. Login (internal) view behaves correctly on the "only types with certs" point, per client.

Code investigation against `Controllers/Api/CertificateTileExternalApiController.cs:528-551` and the internal mirror at `Controllers/Api/CertificateTilesApiController.cs:254-292` confirmed three concrete code defects in the public endpoint's `GetFilters` action:
1. **Subcategory flatten loop** (External `:547-550`): inner `foreach` emits each child cert type as its own filter row alongside its parent. Same pattern present in Internal `:285-292` — latent there since login view consumes it identically.
2. **Missing `IsActive` guard** on External `:535` Where clause; Internal `:278` has `ct.IsActive && (...)`, External omits it.
3. **Filter logic uses string equality on `CertificationTypeNames`** with no parent→children rollup. Per memory `feedback_certtypes_hierarchy.md` the type table is hierarchical by design (Level + ParentId), so the filter ought to expand a selected parent to `{parent ∪ children}` before matching.

Client's three complaints in one item map cleanly to these three bugs. Symptom "public shows ALL cert types" appears to be a perception consequence of (1) — the subcategory bloat makes the dropdown look larger; the actual visibility filter (`certTypeIds.Contains(ct.Id) || Children.Any(...)`) is the same on both controllers.

Scoped as DEF-167 in `docs/tracking/defect-register.md`. No code changes made — investigation only. Open questions before implementation: (a) drop ALL non-Level-1 entries from the dropdown vs. allow Level-2 parents that have Level-3 children, (b) whether the parent→children rollup should be visible to the user (tooltip / "+subcategories" label) or silent. Going with `ParentId == null` only and silent rollup unless client weighs in.

Related backlog items in same family: QC #128 (LEED filter shows certs without LEED tag) and QC #149 (L2/L3 Product Category options don't filter). Worth re-checking those for the same root-cause pattern when DEF-167 is implemented.

## 2026-05-07 — DEF-161 /Certificate/Create Product ID validation: lowercase ASIN blocked + server skipped format validation on save

Shawn flagged "validation issues" on `https://gccwebapp.com/Certificate/Create` — couldn't enter a Product ID that passed validation, suspected the issue was global. Reproduced on localhost with a Playwright pass against every Product ID type (`B08N5WRWNW`, `b08n5wrwnw`, `036000291452`, `4006381333931`, `9780306406157`, `SKU-12345`, etc.). Two defects under the one symptom:

1. **Client ASIN regex was case-sensitive** (`product-id-manager.js:861`). Typing `b08n5wrwnw` got "ASIN must be exactly 10 alphanumeric characters" — the message didn't say *uppercase*, so users had no recovery hint. SKU and MPN regexes already had the `/i` flag; ASIN was the lone outlier. Server `ProductIdService.ValidateAsin` had the same case-sensitive pattern.
2. **`CertificateController.Create` POST persisted Product IDs without running format validation** at all — only the Edit-time `/api/productids` round-trip called `ProductIdService.ValidateProductIdAsync`. `Edit` POST had the same gap. Net effect: a malformed Product ID could be saved through the form path even if the client check were bypassed.

Fix is a single normalisation rule applied at every save boundary:
- Client: ASIN regex now case-insensitive; new `normalizeProductIdValue` uppercases ASIN/UPC/GTIN/EAN/ISBN/SKU/MPN values before push to in-memory list.
- Server: new `ProductIdService.NormalizeValueForType` helper, applied inside `ValidateProductIdAsync`, `CreateProductIdAsync`, `UpdateProductIdAsync`, and `ImportProductIdsAsync` (bulk CSV).
- Server: Create POST and Edit POST both run a pre-validation pass — canonicalise type+value, then `ValidateProductIdAsync` each row, raising `ModelState["ProductIds[i].ProductIdValue"]` errors for invalid entries so the form re-renders with inline errors instead of silently saving.

Verified locally:
- Validation truth table (`verify-isbn.mjs`): `asin_lower` and `asin_mixed` flipped from `false` to `true` after fix; all other types unchanged.
- Server `/api/productids/validate` (`verify-server.mjs`): lowercase ASIN now returns `data: true`; bad value still `data: false`.
- End-to-end Create (`e2e-create.mjs`): submitted `b08abc1234` (lowercase) on a new cert; redirect to `/Certificate/CertificateInternalView/26-0158`. Direct SQL: `ASIN | B08ABC1234` — canonicalised on save.

Files: `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js`, `Services/ProductIdService.cs`, `Controllers/CertificateController.cs`. DEF-161 in `docs/tracking/defect-register.md`. Entry in `docs/tracking/shipped-2026-05.md`.

## 2026-05-07 - QC #58 answer to Carly: cert numbering + draft model + form recovery

Carly's question on the cert Create timeout: *"is that draft user specific or would the draft save for all logged in internal users because that would be the next cert # available?"* Mashed together three different things; clarified each:

1. **Cert numbers are not reserved at form-open.** `CertificateController.Create` (line 287) calls `_certificateRepository.GenerateNextCertificateNumberAsync()`, which is a pure read — `MAX(Number) + 1` for the current year against the `Certificates` table (`Repositories/CertificateRepository.cs:704-718`). Number is shown in the field but only locked in when the row writes on Submit. Two analysts opening Create simultaneously both see the same proposed number; first to submit wins.
2. **Drafts are not user-specific.** A "Draft" is just `Certificate.Status = "Draft"` — a normal database row visible to all internal Admin/Analyst users. There is no per-user scratch / Save-As-Draft store. If you want something to persist before all required fields are filled, that would be a separate CR.
3. **Form-clearing was idle session timeout.** `Program.cs:31` session `IdleTimeout = 30 min`, `Program.cs:245` auth cookie `ExpireTimeSpan = 30 min` with `SlidingExpiration = true`. "Remember Me" only persists login across browser restarts (14 days) — it does not extend idle timeout while a form sits open. After 30 min idle, the anti-forgery token is stale and POST drops the form.
4. **There is no form recovery today.** `wwwroot/js/certificate-create.js:705` has `SHOW_RECOVERY_PROMPT: false` — banner gated off in DEF-151 with auto-save still writing silently to localStorage and stale entries GC'd at 2 hr so storage doesn't leak. Recovery banner is filed as **CR-017 (Phase 2)** per Shawn's call 2026-05-07; not a launch blocker. Originally I told Carly the banner exists — that was wrong; corrected.

QC #58 stays in **Working as Designed** in `qc-sprint-3-reconciliation-2026-05-04.md:151`. CR-017 detail in `change-request-register.md:206` and `docs/tracking/CR-017-form-recovery-ux.md`.

## 2026-05-05 - DEF-146: Product ID Manager "Created By" preserved on cert edit

Shawn reported `gccwebapp.com/Certificate/Edit/26-0147` showing "Created By = System" on every Product ID row. Two-bug interaction: (1) `CertificateController.Edit` POST cleared and re-added the entire `ProductIds` collection on every save, hardcoding `CreatedBy = currentUserId` on every row in the loop — overwriting the original creator on every cert edit; (2) prod cert 26-0147 already had `CreatedBy = NULL` in the DB (likely a legacy state), and `wwwroot/js/product-id-manager.js:244` falls back to literal `"System"` when `createdByUser` is null.

Fix replaces clear-and-readd with merge: existing rows keep their `CreatedBy/CreatedAt`, only get `UpdatedBy/UpdatedAt` stamped; new rows (Id==0) get `CreatedBy = currentUserId`; rows the user deleted in the UI are removed by Id-set diff. Backfill of existing NULL rows on prod is **out of scope** — real-record data UPDATEs need a CR from GCC.

Verified locally on `localhost:5101` / `GCCDatabase_Dev` via Playwright (`C:\Users\swest\AppData\Local\Temp\uitest\test-pid-createdby.js`): three scenarios — preserve NULL on plain edit, preserve admin while analyst saves, new row gets analyst while existing rows keep admin — all PASS.
